short: Metal-Organic Framework Cathodes Based on a Vanadium Hexacya
title: Metal-Organic Framework Cathodes Based on a Vanadium Hexacyanoferrate Prussian Blue Analogue for High-Performance Aqueous Rechargeable Batteries

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Aqueous Prussian blue analogue cathodes have been stuck at 50-65 mA h/g. A framework in which both metal sites are redox active should give multi-electron capacity, if it can be made crystalline enough.
states.detail: Absorbed: n2 (HYP/gap), n3 (HYP/hypothesis), n4 (DES/base_system), n5 (DES/route), n6 (DES/variable_sweep), n7 (DES/method), n8 (PRC/synthesis), n9 (PRC/stimulus), n14 (DES/down_select)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: All three powders are the cubic V3[Fe(CN)6]2 phase (PDF 00-042-1440). Crystallinity ranks co-precipitation with HCl above without HCl above simple mixing.
states.detail: Absorbed: n10 (STR/phase/identity), n12 (STR/phase/fraction), n16 (STR/chemistry/composition). Premises: K-edge energy position maps to oxidation state through the FeO/Fe2O3 and V2O3/VO2/V2O5 reference spectra

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Discharge capacity 91 mA h/g at 110 mA/g, far above a single-electron PBA. Two redox centres in one framework transfer more than one electron per formula unit, which is where the extra capacity comes from.
states.detail: Absorbed: n15 (PRP/value), n17 (MEC/pathway), n18 (PRP/value), n19 (MEC/pathway), n20 (PRP/value)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: The cathode is a candidate for large-scale aqueous stationary storage

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: A dual-redox V/Fe framework, made crystalline by acidified co-precipitation, delivers 91 mA h/g in an aqueous cell

use: The results of the rate study demonstrated the high power performance of the V/Fe PBA-based cathodes; a delivered capacity of $5 7 \%$ was still utilized under an extremely high current density of The potential profiles at selected cycles with different current densities are shown in Figure 4B.

10.1002/aenm.201601491#F5c.definition: Nyquist plots evolved during cycling measured at the fully charged state at 1.15 V. The observed data and simulated curves corresponding to the equivalent circuit model (inset) are denoted as open circles and dotted lines, respectively
use: Figure 6C presents Nyquist plots of the observed data (open circles) and simulated curves (dotted lines) as a function of the cycle number.
The observed result was simulated using the equivalent circuit shown in the inset of Figure 6C.

Additionally, Figure S6B,C in the Supporting Information depicts the comparison of the simulation accuracy of the observed data with different types of equivalent circuit models and confirms that the model shown in the inset of Figure 6C suitably reflects the measured data.

use: The calculated resistance components as a function of the cycle number are shown in Figure 6D. $R _ { \mathrm { e } }$ was independent of the cycle number because the galvanostatic cycling was conducted within a stable potential region of the aqueous electrolyte, which was supported by an absence of the current tail vicinity of the lower and upper potential limits of the CVs.
